thread:
jordan: Heads-up — I just saw a user with the Viewer role get the Edit button on the Project settings page. Repro steps: login as viewer -> open /console/projects/abc -> click settings -> Edit button visible. Screenshot: https://img.internal/rndx/permbug.png

sarah: whoa. any idea if it's a UI-only rendering bug or an actual permission leak server-side?

mike: quick grep of server logs for that user shows the returned permission bundle includes editor flags. snippet from auth-service:
```
2025-11-02T18:12:04.321Z INFO auth: user=team_viewer123 roles=[viewer] perm_bundle={can_edit:false, can_manage_keys:false}
2025-11-02T18:12:04.322Z INFO auth: serialize_perm_bundle -> perm_string="can_manage_keys=false;can_edit=false"
2025-11-02T18:12:04.323Z WARN auth: perm_deserialize mismatch, fallback to string parse -> roles_deser=[viewer,editor]
```

mike: so looks like deserialize produced [viewer,editor] even though roles=[viewer] upstream.

claire: that smells like non-deterministic ordering in the perm serialization. If the perm_string is built from a map without stable keys, our naive parse can accidentally combine flags from stale caches.

jordan: reproduction on local: toggling feature flag `enable_perm_cache_v2` flips repro on/off. with flag off, no edit button. with flag on, edit appears.

alex: security note — we need to assume this is an access-control defect until proven UI-only. Capture audit trail for impacted users and projects. Also, KMS call logs for any key-modifying APIs invoked by those sessions.

mike: checked KMS audit for that timeframe — interestingly, requests to /projects/abc/keys returned 200 but KMS logs show anonymous principal in 3 entries (key_id missing). sample: 
```
2025-11-02T18:12:05Z kms-audit: request_id=Z12a user= - key_id= - action=getKey policy_evaluated=allow
```

mike: suggests our auth middleware returned a perm allowing read-of-keys but KMS didn't get proper principal metadata.

claire: provisional root cause hypothesis: cache v2 serializes permission bitset into a semicolon-delimited string; when code path A writes, insertion order differs and parser incorrectly maps positional tokens to permission enums. Result: a false positive editor bit. Fix: switch to JSON-encoded stable object with explicit keys or include versioned header.

jordan: can we patch quickly? a minimal fix would be to add a defensive check in the UI to hide Edit unless server explicitly returns can_edit=true (not derived). but that's bandaid.

claire: agreed. I'll open a hotfix PR to server to make serializer stable and add a compatibility layer to reject malformed perm_strings (log + 401 for ambiguous). PR link: https://phab.internal/D1234

alex: also create an incident ticket and notify customers impacted by project-abc scope. We should rotate any keys that had anonymous KMS access as precaution.

mike: deploying a canary build to staging now with the stable serializer. deploy-bot: starting rollout canary->staging.

deploy-bot: deploy started: auth-service v3.8.4-canary to staging (instances=2). CI: passed, migrations: none.

jordan: @claire please add logging to surface the exact perm_string value and parser tokenization for audit — but ensure PII/KMS key_id redaction.

claire: will do. Also adding a smoke test that enumerates role permutations and asserts idempotent serialize(deserialize(role_set)).

alex: next steps checklist: 1) collect impacted sessions (mike), 2) canary + verify no anonymous KMS entries (mike + ops), 3) hotfix rollout to prod with one-hour maintenance window (claire), 4) rotate any exposed keys (security), 5) customer outreach draft (CS).

jordan: thanks all. I'll start a short incident note and tag CS. Keeping this thread for updates. :eyes:
